transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-27
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Myers (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Liam O'Neill (Redwood Channel), Maya Lopez (Redwood CSM); Sara Kim (NewBridge Head of Partnerships), Owen Martinez (NewBridge Sales Dir), Ruth Alvarez (NewBridge Solutions Architect)

Summary: Quick pipeline review focused on co-sell motion, three priority deals, next steps for joint GTM, and benchmarking ask. Discussed alignment on logos, pricing expectations, pilot timelines, and documentation/security checklist.

Topics: pipeline highlights, deal owners, technical readiness, security/compliance asks, joint marketing/GTM, next steps.

[00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): Hey everybody, thanks for joining, appreciate you carving out the time. Quick who you are in chat if you haven't yet.
[00:18] Sara (NewBridge): Hi all, Sara here, Head of Partnerships. We'll run through the three deals we flagged last week and talk timing.
[00:25] Jordan: Awesome. Priya from the SE team is on to cover benchmarks and any technical asks. Liam is here for channel ops and Maya for success planning.
[00:36] Priya (Redwood SE): Hey hi, thanks. I'll drop the benchmark sheet after this call, quick note I have a preliminary latency/cost run on the two model configs you asked about.
[00:47] Owen (NewBridge): Great. The first deal — Acero Health — is the one we're most excited about. It's a pilot for care-coordination assistant, potential to expand to 30k monthly active users after Q3.
[01:02] Ruth (NewBridge): Tech contact there is already asking about VPC option and on-prem; they have PHI concerns, so private deployment is a must unless we can guarantee encryption at rest + strict audit logs.
[01:18] Jordan: Understood. For PHI we usually recommend Redwood Private with KMS integration; we can also do a Dedicated pool with encryption and SOC2 controls if they need it in cloud. We'll share the security pack.
[01:33] Sara: Timing on that? They want pilot by mid-May.
[01:37] Priya: From the SE perspective, mid-May pilot is doable if we start integration in early April. We'll need initial endpoints, sample prompts, and some representative data profiles. Also need to validate latency SLOs — they want sub-300ms tail for short responses.
[01:53] Jordan: On pricing, NewBridge said they're flexible but they expect competitive co-sell margins — they asked for a joint discount structure. Owen, are you comfortable with a pilot discount?
[02:03] Owen: Yes, pilot discount for first 3 months is fine but they want clarity on per-token and any add-on charges for Private.
[02:12] Jordan: We'll include a clear line item for Private deployment setup and monthly reserved capacity if applicable.
[02:20] Liam (Channel): Also want to call out our referral fee tiers; if this goes to expansion we have a scaled co-sell commission. I'll circulate the partner comp doc.
[02:31] Sara: Perfect. Deal two is Meridian Retail — lower security bar but high throughput, heavy embedding use for product search. They care about cost more than latency.
[02:44] Priya: For embeddings-heavy workloads we usually suggest quantized models and batching — Redwood Optimize recommendations can reduce cost 30-50% depending on profile. I'll include model / quant suggestions in the sheet.
[02:56] Ruth: Any known competitors in that space NewBridge is worried about?
[02:59] Owen: They're evaluating MegaCloud AI and InferShift — price was a deciding factor last time.
[03:07] Jordan: Ok we'll highlight cost-per-query comparisons and a case study for a retailer with similar scale.
[03:13] Sara: Deal three is Zenith Logistics — long-term pilot with potential for Dedicated capacity. They want an SLA and predictable throughput.
[03:23] Priya: For Dedicated we can propose baseline throughput numbers; to get the SLA we need a 6-12 week onboarding and baseline traffic profile. What's their timeline?
[03:32] Sara: Q3 pilot start, decision in June.
[03:36] Jordan: Sounds aligned. A few security/compliance items came up in earlier emails — SSO/SAML, audit logs, and data residency. Ruth, can you confirm which of these are must-haves for each account?
[03:47] Ruth: Acero is strict: SAML+SCIM, KMS with customer-managed keys, and audit logs retained 1 year. Meridian wants only SSO, and Zenith wants region preference (EU).
[03:58] Jordan: We'll prepare the security checklist doc and mark which items are covered by Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. We'll also attach SOC2 and ISO summaries.
[04:09] Maya (Redwood CSM): On onboarding: if Acero goes Private, we should start their onboarding plan now — allocate a CSM and schedule a technical kick-off in early April.
[04:20] Owen: Agreed. I can intro the Acero IT lead next week.
[04:24] [05:00] Priya: Quick note on benchmarks — my preliminary numbers: hosted default gen config (gpt-like open model) gives 120-180ms median, tail ~260-320ms depending on prompt size; Dedicated with optimized kernels drops tail under 220ms for our test prompts. For embeddings quantized run shows token-cost improvements but you see a small quality delta for nearest-neighbor recall in edge cases.
[05:30] Ruth: That quality delta — can you run a small eval on our sample product catalog for Meridian? They want to see recall hit-rate.
[05:39] Priya: Yep, send sample and we'll run a 500-query eval. I'll include precision/recall numbers in the sheet.
[05:46] Jordan: On go-to-market, Liam, what co-marketing assets do we have ready?
[05:51] Liam: We have a partner one-pager, joint case study template, and a playbook for co-sell motions. I'll attach the partner playbook and we can co-brand it. Also propose a webinar in May to generate inbound leads.
[06:03] Sara: Webinar is interesting — can we co-host and have a case study panel?
[06:07] Jordan: Yes, we can do joint panel — we'll need a committed case and a PR plan. 
[06:12] Owen: Also, for contract/legal: Acero's procurement asked about indemnity and data processing addendums. Do we have a redwood standard DPA?
[06:21] Jordan: Yes, we do. We'll share the DPA and our standard MSA; for Private deployments we usually add the KMS annex and a scope doc. 
[06:31] Ruth: Any blockers for Acero to sign quick pilot? They want proof of logging and encryption.
[06:36] Priya: We can provide demo logs and sample audit output from a recent customer (sanitized). That should satisfy their security team for pilot sign-off.
[06:45] [08:00] Jordan: Ok let's run through owners and dates real quick: Jordan sends updated GTM deck by Monday (3/29). Priya shares benchmark and latency/cost spreadsheet by Friday (4/2). Ruth to provide top 3 pilot account contacts by 4/5. Owen to coordinate exec intro by 4/1. Liam to share partner comp doc and one-pager by 3/30. Maya to draft onboarding plan if Acero selects Private and schedule kick-off for week of April 6th.
[08:30] Sara: That timeline works for us, though Acero wants pilot paperwork in hand sooner — they'd like to start contract review by April 10.
[08:38] Jordan: We'll accelerate the DPA + pilot SOW drafting and circulate a redline by April 6.
[08:44] Ruth: A quick technical ask — can we surface per-request debug logs for Acero's devs? They want to troubleshoot model outputs quickly in the pilot.
[08:53] Priya: We have per-request tracing and optional payload redaction. For PHI we redact PII by default on hosted but for Private we can ship full traces to their logging endpoint with customer consent. We'll outline options.
[09:05] Owen: Pricing expectation — Acero expects a blended pilot rate with a setup fee. Any ballpark?
[09:12] Jordan: For pilots that include Private work we usually do a modest setup fee (~$15k) plus discounted per-token for first 90 days. We'll put numbers in the GTM deck.
[09:21] [10:00] Sara: Meridian — is there anything we need from Salesforce/opps side to push them? They want usage-based contract but with a capped monthly spend.
[10:31] Liam: We can propose a consumption contract with a soft cap and an overage rate. I'll work with Jordan on the contract language.
[10:40] Ruth: One more technical note — Zenith wants regional residency (EU). Is Private the only option?
[10:48] Priya: We can host in EU region on Dedicated or Private. If they insist on customer-managed keys in EU, that's Private. We'll clarify options in the doc.
[10:58] Jordan: Good. Any other competitor intel?
[11:02] Owen: MegaCloud AI quoted lower per-token but their latencies and support levels were variable. InferShift was pricier but offered a prebuilt search plugin.
[11:12] Jordan: We'll lean into reliability and observability as differentiators — Redwood Console demos on token-level costs and tracing usually help procurement.
[11:21] Sara: For next meeting, can we do a short technical runbook review with Acero's devs plus our SE? Say 45 minutes early April?
[11:29] Priya: Yes, we'll set that up. Send possible times.
[11:33] Jordan: I'll propose slots in the shared calendar.
[11:36] [48:00] Closing recap: Jordan: Action items as discussed: GTM deck (Jordan), benchmarks (Priya), partner comp doc (Liam), pilot contacts (Ruth), exec intro (Owen), onboarding plan (Maya). We'll target a follow-up next Wednesday (2026-04-01) for exec intro alignment.
[48:25] Sara: Thanks everyone, this was helpful.
[48:29] Owen: Thanks, talk soon.
[48:33] Priya: I'll start the benchmark runs today.
[48:36] Jordan: Thanks all, meeting adjourned.
